newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BankWest says annual profit could fall.
newsitem.headline: BankWest says annual profit could fall.

text.p: Bank of Western Australia Ltd repeated on Wednesday that 1997/98 (March-February) earnings are likely to be below last year due to competitive pressures.

"The directors believe that the bank will find it difficult but not impossible to achieve in the current year the level of profits achieved in the financial year just ended," chairman Ian Mackenzie said at the annual general meeting.
"I should also caution you that the effect of restructuring costs and the adjustments to lower margins are likely to be felt more heavily in the first half of the current year," Mackenzie said.

The regional bank, which is 51.47 percent-owned by Bank of Scotland, achieved a 1996/97 net profit of A$94.5 million compared with its prospectus forecast of A$100.2 million. At the time of the results announcement, it said the profit level might not be sustainable.

Mackenzie said the prospectus forecast was prepared in December 1995 before the Reserve Bank undertook a concerted monetary policy easing which resulted in four cuts of 50 basis points each in the official cash rate. He said the scope of these reductions and the decline in interest margins could not have been predicted. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
